elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires each Servicer and Marketing Agent to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence.

elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 in the aggregate.

elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000.

elements.element: Each Vendor that processes Customer Data must maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires $5,000,000 of cyber liability insurance only while a Servicer or Marketing Agent holds, processes, or accesses Personally Identifiable Information of Obligors. That trigger is narrower than processing any Customer Data, and the stated coverage is only cyber liability rather than expressly cyber/privacy coverage.

elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law.

elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must provide certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires the Servicer and Marketing Agent to deliver certificates evidencing the coverage to the Issuer, Depositor, and Indenture Trustee on request.

elements.element: Each applicable Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative $2,000,000 professional liability limit exceeds the fallback $1,000,000 requirement.

elements.element: Each Vendor that processes Customer Data must maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Although the $5,000,000 amount exceeds the fallback limit, the covenant is triggered only by holding, processing, or accessing Personally Identifiable Information of Obligors and does not expressly cover all processing of Customer Data or require privacy coverage.

result.reason: Neither level is complete because the cyber covenant uses a narrower data trigger and coverage description than required. The amendment also goes beyond the requested position by imposing every coverage for one year after termination and appears to relocate an unrelated Receivables fragment from before Section 6.4 to after Section 10.11, impairing the structure and potentially the meaning of the existing agreement.
